desc:
User import and account migration without resets moves your existing customers into your new app, so nobody has to sign up again. Ecom Swift LLC cleans the data, maps the fields and carries over passwords where the format allows.

## What is a user import?

A user import is a controlled transfer of account records from one place to another. The source may be an old platform, a database export, an API or a spreadsheet. The destination is the user table of your new app, with each person's email, name, plan, role and any other fields you choose.

Done well, customers log in on switch-over day and find everything where they left it.

## Why moving users is risky

A move is a one-time event that is hard to repeat. If it goes wrong, people lose access, receive the wrong email or appear twice. Asking everyone to register again feels like a small cost, but many customers simply never return.

Data quality is the usual obstacle. Exports contain duplicate emails, upper and lower case differences, blank names, old plan labels and test records. Importing them unchanged brings every old problem into the new system.

## How a clean migration protects your customer base

The benefit is continuity. People keep their history, plan and settings, so the change of platform feels like an upgrade rather than a restart. Fewer people need to contact support, and fewer lapse during the transition.

Passwords are a special case. If the old system stores hashes in a format your new app can verify, existing passwords can keep working. Where that is not possible, a friendly set-your-password email lets users create a new one with a single click. We explain which path applies after we see a sample of the data, and we do not promise that every password can move.

## What a great import includes

- A written field map from the old data to the new user table.
- Cleaning of emails: trimming, lower-casing and obvious typo checks.
- Duplicate detection with a clear rule for which record wins.
- Roles, plans and status values translated to your new names.
- Password hashes carried over when compatible, with a fallback email otherwise.
- A test run on a small group before the full import.
- Control over whether users receive an email, and when.
- A result report listing imported, skipped and failed records.
- A backup and rollback plan before any change is made.
- A final sync on switch-over day for accounts created in the meantime.

## What we do

We begin with a sample of your data and a talk about what the new system needs. We then write the mapping and the cleaning rules, and show you the result on a few records before anything is final.

The import runs first in a test environment, then on a small real group, then in full. Each run produces a report so you can check counts and look at exceptions. For larger moves, we plan the switch-over day with you, including a pause on new sign-ups in the old system and a final sync after.

The Basic package covers a one-time import from a file with cleaning, duplicate merging and a report. Standard handles a larger file, password carry-over where possible, set-your-password emails, a trial run and role mapping. Premium handles very large moves, API or live database sources, a final sync, a backup and rollback plan and a handover call.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Take a full backup before importing.
- Run a small test group first.
- Decide your duplicate rule in advance.
- Plan the emails that users will receive.
- Keep the old system available until the switch is confirmed.

**Avoid:**
- Importing without cleaning the data first.
- Sending a flood of emails on the same day.
- Sharing exports through chat or unprotected links.
- Switching off the old system on the day of import.
- Assuming every password format can move across.

## Who this is for

It suits a business moving from one platform or login service to another. It also suits a company that collected customers in a spreadsheet and now has a real app, or one that is merging two products. A store or community adding member accounts for existing buyers is another case.

## What we need from you

Send a small sample of the data first, with names changed if you prefer, and a description of the source system and the new user table. We need collaborator or developer access to the new project and a staging environment, and we can receive the full export through a secure method you choose. We never need passwords, and we delete our copies of your data when the work is complete.
